ei.title: Chapter 5-15: The Danger of Workplace Perfectionism
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Many people excuse perfectionism at work by claiming it is professionalism. Differentiating between the two is useful. Managing perfectionism does not mean dropping critical standards. It becomes a problem when your personal expectations become unmanageable, self-imposed demands that create more pressure than is needed. It is not permission for work sloppiness or low standards; rather it means spending less time on tasks that do not need the level of input you are providing. What are the acceptable standards of professionalism in your work and how do these compare with your own? With the busyness of workplaces these days, trying to achieve a benchmark of 110% perfect on everything can be a recipe for burnout. If you are a manager expecting this of others, you may be setting yourself up for failure.

questions.passage: Many people (A)[excuse / condemn] perfectionism at work by claiming it is professionalism. Differentiating between the two is useful. Managing perfectionism does not mean (B)[keeping / dropping] critical standards. It becomes a problem when your personal expectations become unmanageable, self-imposed demands that create more pressure than is needed. It is not permission for work sloppiness or low standards; rather it means spending less time on tasks that do not need the level of input you are providing. What are the acceptable standards of professionalism in your work and how do these compare with your own? With the busyness of workplaces these days, trying to achieve a benchmark of 110% perfect on everything can be a recipe for (C)[burnout / success]. If you are a manager expecting this of others, you may be setting yourself up for failure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 완벽주의를 변명하고, 기준을 포기하는 것을 의미하지 않으며, 번아웃의 지름길.
det.analysis:
✅ ① excuse — dropping — burnout — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② condemn (A 반대: 변명하다→비난하다)
❌ ③ keeping (B 반대: 포기하다→유지하다)
❌ ④ success (C 반대: 번아웃→성공)

questions.passage: Many people excuse perfectionism at work by claiming it is professionalism. Differentiating between the two is (A)[useful / pointless]. Managing perfectionism does not mean dropping critical standards. It becomes a problem when your personal expectations become (B)[controllable / unmanageable], self-imposed demands that create more pressure than is needed. It is not permission for work sloppiness or low standards; rather it means spending less time on tasks that do not need the level of input you are providing. What are the (C)[acceptable / objectionable] standards of professionalism in your work and how do these compare with your own? With the busyness of workplaces these days, trying to achieve a benchmark of 110% perfect on everything can be a recipe for burnout. If you are a manager expecting this of others, you may be setting yourself up for failure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 둘을 구분하는 것은 유용하고, 기대치가 제어 불가능해지며, 허용되는 기준.
det.analysis:
❌ ① pointless (A 반대: 유용한→무의미한)
❌ ② controllable (B 반대: 제어 불가능한→제어 가능한)
✅ ③ useful — unmanageable — acceptable — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ objectionable (C 반대: 허용되는→받아들일 수 없는)
det.tip: useful(유용한)↔pointless(무의미한), unmanageable(제어 불가능한)↔controllable(제어 가능한), acceptable(허용되는)↔objectionable(받아들일 수 없는)

questions.passage: Many people excuse perfectionism at work by claiming it is professionalism. Differentiating between the two is useful. Managing perfectionism does not mean dropping critical standards. It becomes a problem when your personal expectations become unmanageable, self-imposed demands that create more pressure than is needed. It is not permission for work sloppiness or low standards; rather it means spending (A)[less / more] time on tasks that do not need the level of input you are providing. What are the acceptable standards of professionalism in your work and how do these compare with your own? With the busyness of workplaces these days, trying to achieve a benchmark of 110% (B)[flawed / perfect] on everything can be a recipe for burnout. If you are a manager expecting this of others, you may be setting yourself up for (C)[failure / success].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 시간을 더 적게 쓰고, 110% 완벽, 실패를 자초할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① more (A 반대: 더 적게→더 많이)
✅ ② less — perfect — failure — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ flawed (B 반대: 완벽한→결함 있는)
❌ ④ success (C 반대: 실패→성공)
det.tip: less(더 적은)↔more(더 많은), perfect(완벽한)↔flawed(결함 있는), failure(실패)↔success(성공)

questions.passage: Many people ①<u>excuse</u> perfectionism at work by claiming it is professionalism. Differentiating between the two is ②<u>useless</u>. Managing perfectionism does not mean dropping ③<u>critical</u> standards. It becomes a problem when your personal expectations become unmanageable, self-imposed demands that create more pressure than is needed. It is not permission for work sloppiness or low standards; rather it means spending less time on tasks that do not need the level of input you are providing. What are the acceptable standards of professionalism in your work and how do these compare with your own? With the busyness of workplaces these days, trying to achieve a benchmark of 110% perfect on everything can be a recipe for ④<u>burnout</u>. If you are a manager expecting this of others, you may be setting yourself up for failure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 완벽주의와 전문성을 구분하는 것이 유용하다(useful)는 맥락이므로 useless는 부적절.
det.analysis:
① <u>excuse</u> (변명하다) — 완벽주의를 전문성이라며 변명, 적절

② <u>useless</u> (쓸모없는) — 원문 useful(유용한). 둘을 구분하는 것이 유용하다는 맥락에서 useless 부적절 ←정답

③ <u>critical</u> (중대한) — 중대한 기준을 포기하지 않음, 적절

④ <u>burnout</u> (번아웃) — 번아웃의 지름길, 적절

questions.passage: Many people excuse perfectionism at work by ①<u>claiming</u> it is professionalism. Differentiating between the two is useful. Managing perfectionism does not mean dropping critical standards. It becomes a problem when your personal expectations become unmanageable, self-imposed demands that create more ②<u>pressure</u> than is needed. It is not permission for work sloppiness or low standards; rather it means spending ③<u>more</u> time on tasks that do not need the level of input you are providing. What are the acceptable standards of professionalism in your work and how do these compare with your own? With the busyness of workplaces these days, trying to achieve a benchmark of 110% perfect on everything can be a recipe for burnout. If you are a manager expecting this of others, you may be setting yourself up for ④<u>failure</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 완벽주의를 관리하는 것은 불필요한 일에 시간을 더 적게(less) 쓰는 것이므로 more는 부적절.
det.analysis:
① <u>claiming</u> (주장하며) — 전문성이라고 주장하며 변명, 적절

② <u>pressure</u> (압박) — 필요 이상의 압박을 만듦, 적절

③ <u>more</u> (더 많이) — 원문 less(더 적게). 완벽주의 관리는 불필요한 업무에 시간을 더 적게 쓰는 것이므로 more 부적절 ←정답

④ <u>failure</u> (실패) — 실패를 자초할 수 있음, 적절
det.tip: spending less time(더 적게)↔more time(더 많이)

What are the acceptable standards of professionalism in your work and how do these compare with your own? With the busyness of workplaces these days, trying to achieve a ③<u>benchmark</u> of 110% perfect on everything can be a recipe for burnout. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 완벽주의가 문제가 되는 것은 기대치가 '제어 불가능해질(unmanageable)' 때이므로 manageable은 부적절.
det.analysis:
① <u>manageable</u> (제어 가능한) — 원문 unmanageable(제어 불가능한). 기대치가 제어 불가능해질 때 문제가 되므로 manageable 부적절 ←정답

② <u>permission</u> (허용) — 일을 대충 하는 것에 대한 허용이 아님, 적절

③ <u>benchmark</u> (기준) — 110% 완벽이라는 기준, 적절

④ <u>failure</u> (실패) — 실패를 자초, 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 기대치가 '제어 불가능해질' 때 문제가 된다.
det.analysis: manage → unmanageable. become 뒤 보어 자리에 형용사가 필요하고, '제어 불가능한'이라는 부정 의미이므로 un- + manage + -able = unmanageable.

questions.passage: Many people excuse perfectionism at work by claiming it is professionalism. Differentiating between the two is useful. Managing perfectionism does not mean dropping critical standards. It becomes a problem when your personal expectations become unmanageable, self-imposed demands that __________. It is not permission for work sloppiness or low standards; rather it means spending less time on tasks that do not need the level of input you are providing. What are the acceptable standards of professionalism in your work and how do these compare with your own? With the busyness of workplaces these days, trying to achieve a benchmark of 110% perfect on everything can be a recipe for burnout. If you are a manager expecting this of others, you may be setting yourself up for failure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 스스로 부과한 요구는 '필요 이상의 압박을 만들어 낸다'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① guarantee much higher quality work (더 높은 품질 보장) — 글의 요지와 반대
❌ ② reduce everyone's daily workload (업무량 감소) — 반대
✅ ③ create more pressure than is needed (필요 이상의 압박을 만든다) — 문제의 원인 ←정답
❌ ④ improve team communication a lot (팀 소통 향상) — 무관
det.tip: self-imposed demands → create more pressure than is needed

ch: create more pressure than is needed

questions.passage: Many people excuse perfectionism at work by claiming it is professionalism. Differentiating between the two is useful. Managing perfectionism does not mean dropping critical standards. It becomes a problem when your personal expectations become unmanageable, self-imposed demands that create more pressure than is needed. It is not permission for work sloppiness or low standards; rather it means spending less time on tasks that do not need the level of input you are providing. What are the acceptable standards of professionalism in your work and how do these compare with your own? With the busyness of workplaces these days, trying to achieve a benchmark of 110% perfect on everything __________. If you are a manager expecting this of others, you may be setting yourself up for failure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 모든 일에 110% 완벽을 추구하는 것은 '번아웃으로 가는 지름길일 수 있다'.
det.analysis:
✅ ① can be a recipe for burnout (번아웃의 지름길일 수 있다) — 과도한 완벽 추구의 결과 ←정답
❌ ② always leads to career success (항상 성공으로 이어진다) — 반대
❌ ③ is required of every employee (모든 직원에게 요구된다) — 근거 없음
❌ ④ makes everyday work much easier (업무를 쉽게 만든다) — 반대
det.tip: a recipe for burnout = 번아웃으로 가는 지름길

ch: can be a recipe for burnout
